artworks.title: Minerva and Cecrops
artworks.artist: Cornelis Bloemaert after Pietro da Cortona
artworks.description: Bloemaert after Cortona: Athena with Cecrops — Actaeus' son-in-law who inherits Attica when the first king's line passes through marriage.

artworks.title: Cecrops on an Attic Red-Figure Cup (Birth of Erichthonius)
artworks.description: Berlin cup: Cecrops at Erichthonius' birth — the successor Pausanias sets after Actaeus, first king of the land once called Actaea.

artworks.title: West Pediment of the Parthenon: Cecrops and Pandrosus
artworks.description: Parthenon west pediment marbles: Cecrops' house on the Acropolis — the Athenian foundation story that begins, in Pausanias' roll, with Actaeus before Cecrops.

popCulture.title: Actaeus
popCulture.description: First king of Attica in Pausanias' native roll — ruler of Actaea before Cecrops marries his daughter and takes the throne.

popCulture.title: Cecrops I
popCulture.description: Actaeus' successor by marriage — the snake-bodied founder who overshadows the first king in later Athenian memory.

popCulture.title: Attica
popCulture.description: The land once called Actaea after Actaeus — the eponym as Attica's oldest royal name.

popCulture.title: Description of Greece
popCulture.creator: Pausanias
popCulture.description: Pausanias' Attic king-list opens with Actaeus — the antiquarian first name before Cecrops.
